question: You intend to turn right at the junction. Are you obliged to give way to vehicles approaching from the left?
options: Yes
No
explanation:
Traffic signals always take priority over road signs. The road sign indicating the
obligation to give way only applies if the traffic signals are not functioning.
“An instruction by means of a non-flashing light at a traffic signal applies ahead of
an instruction concerning an obligation to stop or an obligation to give way that is
provided by means of a road sign.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
Green (SIG3)

question: How many lanes does this road have?
options: 0 lanes.
1 lane.
2 lanes.
4 lanes.
explanation:
Lane: “A longitudinal field on a carriageway shown by road markings or, if there
are no road markings, that is wide enough for traffic in one file of four-wheeled
vehicles”. (Ordinance on Road Traffic Definitions)
Because there are no road markings, you must use your own judgement. In this
example, it is clear that there is sufficient room for 2 cars to be driven alongside each
other. The road could perhaps be wide enough for 4 cars, but they would not be able
to be driven in a normal or safe manner.
You can interpret “wide enough for traffic in one file of four-wheeled vehicles” as
meaning that there must be reasonable safety margins between the vehicles, and not
that the vehicles are packed closely together with just 10 cm between them.

question: Do you have an obligation to give way to vehicles coming from the right?
options: Yes
No
explanation:
Vehicles coming from the right are exiting a ‘home zone’. This means that they have
an obligation to give way to you. The priority-to-the-right rule does not therefore
apply.
Home zone (E9)
“A driver also has an obligation to give way to any vehicle when its path crosses
their own path when the driver joins a road [...] from [...] a home zone.” (Road
Traffic Ordinance)

question: Are you obliged to give way to road-users who are already on, or are about to enter, the bicycle crossing?
options: Yes, I must give way to cyclists and drivers of class II mopeds.
Yes, I must give way to cyclists, but I am not obliged to give way to drivers of class II mopeds.
No, because the bicycle crossing is before the roundabout.
No, but I must adapt my speed so that I do not endanger cyclists or moped drivers who are on the bicycle crossing.
explanation:
Bicycle crossing (B8)
“At a bicycle crossing, a driver has an obligation to give way to cyclists and drivers
of class II mopeds who are on, or are just about to enter, the bicycle crossing.”
(Road Traffic Ordinance)

question: Do you have an obligation to give way to vehicles coming from A?
options: Yes, to all vehicles.
Yes, but only to motor vehicles.
No, because the priority-to-the-right rule applies.
No, because I am driving on a priority road.
explanation:
Roundabout (D3)
“A driver who is entering a roundabout is obliged to give way to every vehicle that
is already driving on the roundabout.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)

question: You park your car here at 16.54 on a Tuesday. What time must you state on the parking disc?
explanation:
“If a parking disc or an equivalent device is used, the stated time shall be set to the
nearest subsequent half-hour, counted from the time at which the parking was
commenced.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
If you commence the parking at 16.54, the nearest subsequent half-hour will be
17.00.

question: You are going to A. Which statement is true?
options: I am allowed to turn left at B.
I am allowed to turn right at C and then cross the road.
I am not allowed to turn into A at all from this direction. I must instead make a turn further down the road and drive back.
explanation:
This is an example of a jughandle turn.
Direction sign when junction turn is prohibited (F2)
“The sign provides preparatory information indicating that it is prohibited to turn
at a junction, but that another direction can be chosen.” (Road Sign Ordinance)

question: Could there be intersecting traffic on the same level further ahead on this road?
options: Yes, because the road is not a motorway or a clearway.
No, from this point onwards, there will not be any junctions on the same level.
explanation:
Only motorways and clearways are guaranteed to be free from intersecting traffic on
the same level. (Clearways may have oncoming traffic, but not intersecting traffic.)
‘On the same level’ here refers to a regular junction where there is a risk of colliding
with intersecting traffic. Traffic that crosses the road via a bridge is not on the same
level.
Neither of these signs are shown:
 Motorway (E1) Clearway (E3)
The road you are on is a priority road, and just here there is a central barrier. There
may however be junctions on the same level further ahead.

question: You intend to continue straight ahead. Is it prohibited to overtake the bus in conjunction with the pedestrian crossing?
options: Yes
No
explanation:
At an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, you are not permitted to overtake:
“Vehicles or trams may not be overtaken immediately before or on an uncontrolled
pedestrian crossing.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
This pedestrian crossing, however, is controlled:
“A pedestrian crossing is controlled if the traffic is regulated by traffic signals.”
(Ordinance on Road Traffic Definitions)
In other words, overtaking the bus here is not prohibited.
Even though an action is not prohibited, it may still be inappropriate. Pedestrians
could cross against a red light, and if you deem visibility to be poor, the safest option
is to wait to perform the overtaking until after the pedestrian crossing.
(In this example, however, you appear to be receiving help from the bus. When you
reach the pedestrian crossing, the bus will be blocking any pedestrians from stepping
onto the crossing from the right-hand side.)

question: What does this road sign mean?
options: Furthest distance to level crossing.
Shortest distance to level crossing.
explanation:
Distance to level crossing (A38)
”The signs indicate the distance to a level crossing in a three-bar system. The sign
with the three bars is, except for in densely populated areas, erected under one of
the following signs: A35, Level crossing with gates; A36, Level crossing without
gates; or A37, Junction with tramway line. The sign with two bars indicates that it
is two-thirds the distance to the level crossing and the sign with one bar indicates
the last third of the distance.” (Road Sign Ordinance)

question: Which of these signs indicates a pedestrian street?
options: A
B
C
D
explanation:
A: Built-up area (E5) B: Recommended lower speed (E11)
 C: Home zone (E9) D: Pedestrian street (E7)

question: Is compressed snow (snow that has been worn smooth) good or bad, in terms of grip?
options: Good, as the smooth surface of the snow means that the effectiveness of the tyres’ studs is significantly increased.
Bad, as compressed snow can be very slippery.
Good, as loose snow is more slippery than compressed snow.
explanation:
Snow becomes compressed or smooth-worn when it has been subjected to hard
pressure. It is often found at junctions, where many vehicles come to a standstill
before then accelerating.
Compressed snow has many of the same properties as ice – i.e. poor grip. Compare it
to the experience of walking in deep snow – it is more difficult, but there is much less
risk of slipping and losing your grip.

question: Can probability learning be good?
options: Yes, if it means that I am especially cautious in certain situations.
No, probability learning is always negative in traffic.
explanation:
Probability learning means that you use prior experience of a situation to assess
the probability of something happening.
 Good probability learning: You are used to trains passing frequently at a
 railway crossing and you are therefore extra cautious.
 Bad probability learning: You are used to trains passing very rarely at a
 railway crossing and therefore do not look before you cross.

question: What is the limit for aggravated drunk driving?
options: 0.2 per mille of alcohol in the blood.
0.8 per mille of alcohol in the blood.
1.0 per mille of alcohol in the blood.
2.0 per mille of alcohol in the blood.
explanation:
Aggravated drunk driving: “The driver has a blood alcohol concentration of at least
1.0 per mille.” (Road Traffic Offences Act)

question: Could it be prohibited to drive a vehicle when you are tired?
options: Yes, if I am incapable of driving the vehicle in a safe manner.
No, because tiredness cannot be measured.
explanation:
“A vehicle may not be driven by a person who, due to illness, fatigue, intoxication
by alcohol, other stimulants or sedatives, or for other reasons is incapable of
driving the vehicle in a safe manner.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
You are permitted to be tired as long as you are able to drive the vehicle safely. For
this reason, the question is whether it “could” be prohibited, not whether it is always
prohibited (which is not the case).

question: How much of the visual field is made up of central vision?
explanation:
1
 2 2
 Ö
Semicircle: Visual field
Ö: Location of eye
1: Central vision
2: Peripheral vision

question: What does this sign combination mean?
options: Accident-ridden pedestrian crossing.
Pedestrian crossing where people with hearing impairments often cross.
Pedestrian crossing where people with visual impairments often cross.
Controlled pedestrian crossing.
explanation:
Pedestrian crossing (B3)
Visually impaired (T9)
“The panel indicates that people with visual impairments often use the crossing.
This panel always has a yellow background.” (Road Sign Ordinance)

question: Is it true that you are obliged to show consideration to certain road users?
options: No, everyone should be treated equally.
Yes – for example, children, the elderly and people with disabilities.

question: What should your first response be if you accidentally damage a road sign so that other road users cannot see it?
options: Contact the police.
Try to restore the road sign.
Contact the Swedish Transport Administration.
Contact the land owner.
explanation:
“A person who has moved or altered a road sign, road marking, traffic signal or
other traffic device shall immediately restore the device to an adequate condition. If
this is impossible, they shall promptly inform the police or the person who installed
and maintains the device of its condition and take any necessary measures, as
required by the traffic situation.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
It is important that the sign is restored as soon as possible. If it is a give way sign at a
junction, the consequences could otherwise be dire.

question: How fast are you allowed to drive in a light lorry?
options: Max. 70 km/h.
Max. 90 km/h.
Max. 100 km/h.
As fast as indicated by the sign.
explanation:
Maximum speed for light lorries: “The speed limit applicable to the road.” (Swedish
Transport Agency)

question: How is the reaction time affected by worn tyres?
options: It decreases.
It increases by approximately 50%.
It increases by approximately 100%.
It is not affected at all.
explanation:
The reaction time depends solely on the human driver and has nothing to do with the
properties of the car.

question: When driving in winter conditions, do you have to have studded tyres on the trailer if you have studded tyres on your car?
options: Yes.
Only if it is a trailer with brakes.
No.
explanation:
“If the car has studded tyres, a trailer connected to the car must also have studded
tyres when driving in winter conditions.” (Swedish Transport Agency)
If the car has better grip than the trailer, there is a chance that the trailer will keep
going when the car brakes and fold around the car like a folding pocketknife.

question: Which type of tyre entails the greatest risk of aquaplaning?
options: Extra-narrow tyres.
Normal tyres.
Extra-wide tyres.
explanation:
Red = the amount of water that has to be dispersed for the tyres to have contact
with the road.
Wider tyres mean that more water needs to be pushed aside, which leads to a greater
risk of aquaplaning.

question: What is likely to be the problem if the brake pedal feels springy when you apply the brake?
options: A leak in the brake system.
Worn-out brakes.
Air in the brake system.
explanation:
If there is a leak, the pedal will go down slowly (the brake fluid is pushed out). If the
brakes are worn, it will take longer than normal but the pedal will still feel rigid. Air
in the brake system makes the pedal feel springy, as the air moves around the system
unpredictably.

question: Should the airbag on the front passenger seat be activated if a rear-facing child seat is installed there?
options: Yes, always.
Yes, but only if the child is over 3 years old.
No, never.
explanation:
If the airbag triggers, this will push the child safety seat against the front seat with
great force. The child will be exposed to a great impact, and there is also a risk that
the child may become trapped against the front seat.
Please note that the question says activated (that is: on, engaged).

question: At what point is it safe for a child to sit like an adult in a seat without an airbag?
options: When the child is at least 135 cm tall.
When the child is at least 140 cm tall.
When the child is at least 150 cm tall.
explanation:
“All children under 135 centimetres tall shall be put in a special protection device in
the car, i.e. a baby car seat, a child safety seat, a booster seat or booster cushion.”
(Swedish Transport Agency)
Please note that the questions says without an airbag. If it is a seat with an airbag,
the correct answer would be 140 cm.

question: 260 cm 40 cm Is it permitted to drive the car on a public road?
options: No, as the width is 260 cm.
No, as the load protrudes 40 cm on one side.
Yes, as the width does not exceed 260 cm.
Yes, as the load does not protrude at all on the other side.
explanation:
“If a motor vehicle or a vehicle coupled to this has a load where either side
protrudes more than 20 centimetres outside the vehicle, or if the vehicle’s width,
including load, exceeds 260 centimetres, [...] the vehicle or a vehicle coupled to this
may only be driven on a private road.” (Road Traffic Ordinance)
Review of the options:
 No, as the width is 260 cm.
 – Wrong, the width may be exactly 260 cm, but not more.
 No, as the load protrudes 40 cm on one side.
 – Correct, according to the quote from the Road Traffic Ordinance.
 Yes, as the width does not exceed 260 cm.
 – Wrong, as this answer implies that it is permitted to drive the car with this
 load.
 Yes, as the load does not protrude at all on the other side.
 – Wrong, as this answer implies that it is permitted to drive the car with this
 load.

question: Is the trailer classed as a light trailer if it is connected to the car?
options: Yes
No
explanation:
With a regular category B licence, you are only allowed to tow a light trailer. The
following count as a light trailer:
 1. Trailer with a maximum total weight of 750 kg.
 2. Trailer where the maximum total weight for car + trailer is 3,500 kg
 (3.5 tonnes).
Does the combined total weight exceed 3.5 tonnes?
2,100 kg + 1,100 kg = 3,200 kg = Under 3.5 tonnes

question: Do you have to turn off your full beam headlights when approaching a train travelling in the opposite direction?
options: Yes, if there is a risk of dazzling the driver.
No, as the full beams of a car do not affect the driver of a train.
explanation:
“Full beam headlights may not be used [...] when meeting an oncoming track-
bound transport [...] if there is a possible risk of dazzling the driver.” (Road Traffic
Ordinance)
The train driver must be able to see the tracks. There could be an elk on the line
further ahead, for example. The driver of the train must then have good visibility in
order to activate the emergency brake.

question: What is the smallest permitted tread depth on winter tyres in winter conditions?
options: 1.0 mm
1.6 mm
3.0 mm
3.2 mm
explanation:
“In winter road conditions during the period 1 December–31 March, the tread
depth must be at least 3 mm.” (Swedish Transport Agency)

question: How often do you have to inspect a car that is more than 5 years old?
options: No later than 6 months after the previous inspection.
No later than 12 months after the previous inspection.
No later than 14 months after the previous inspection.
No later than 24 months after the previous inspection.
explanation:
A new car must be inspected for the first time no later than 3 years
 (36 months) after the month when it was first taken into service.
 The second inspection must be conducted no later than 2 years (24 months)
 after the month in which the first inspection was conducted.
 Subsequent inspections must be conducted no later than 14 months after the
 month in which the most recent inspection was conducted.

question: What does it mean if this symbol lights up on the dashboard?
options: Incorrect oil pressure.
The windscreen washer fluid is running low.
The fuel tank is almost empty.
explanation:
The car’s user manual will tell you what the lights mean. The standard symbol for
incorrect oil pressure is an oil can (slight variations in design may occur).

question: Which statement applies to a vehicle’s off-road status?
options: A vehicle automatically has off-road status if it has not been used for a period of 5 years.
A vehicle automatically has off-road status if the vehicle tax has not been paid.
A vehicle automatically has off-road status if it is the subject of a driving ban.
A vehicle is never automatically given off-road status.
explanation:
“It is a common misconception that a vehicle is automatically given off-road status
if it is subject to a driving ban after missing a roadworthiness test, for example.
That is not the case! A vehicle is never automatically given off-road status – you
are responsible for submitting an off-road notification to us.” (Swedish Transport
Agency)

question: What type of damage is not covered by third-party insurance?
options: Damage to your own vehicle.
Damage to someone else’s vehicle.
Personal injury.
explanation:
“Third-party insurance [...] Note that you are not compensated for [...] damage to
your own vehicle”. (Swedish Transport Agency)

question: Why should you remove a roof box when not using it?
options: It constitutes a traffic hazard, as it may fall down.
It increases air resistance and thereby fuel consumption.
The plastic of the roof box emits harmful particles to the air.
explanation:
“Roof boxes and rails create unnecessary air resistance and slow the car down. A
roof box can increase fuel consumption by more than 1 decilitre for every 10
kilometres travelled.” (Swedish Transport Administration)

question: Which statement is true regarding engine braking?
options: It reduces your fuel consumption.
It increases your fuel consumption.
explanation:
“The point of engine braking is that you can completely turn off the fuel feed while
reducing your speed. Braking less using your foot saves fuel [...] If you let up on the
accelerator completely when the engine is running at above 1,500–1,600 rpm, there
will be no fuel at all delivered to the engine. Once you are down to 1,200–1,300
rpm, the engine starts taking in fuel again. You should therefore shift down before
reaching 1,200–1,300 rpm in order to keep the consumption to zero.” (Swedish
Transport Administration)

question: Which alternative best describes a hybrid car?
options: A car that runs on electricity alone.
A car that runs on electricity and petrol.
A car that uses less than 0.3 litres per ten kilometres travelled.
A car that runs solely on solar energy through the use of solar cells.
explanation:
The most common combination is electric + petrol.

question: Which signs indicate the direction to be followed?
options: A and C only.
B and D only.
All of them.
None of them.
explanation:
Mnemonic rule:
 Diagonal (twisted/slanting) arrows = pass on this side (the arrow indicates the
 correct lane).
 Horizontal/Vertical (straight) arrows = direction to be followed (the arrow
 indicates a direction).

question: Several traffic instructions can apply to the same situation at once. What is the correct order of precedence, from highest to lowest?
options: Road signs, rules, traffic signals, police signals
Police signals, traffic signals, road signs, rules
Traffic signals, police signals, rules, road signs
Rules, road signs, traffic signals, police signals
explanation: The book lists the precedence as: 1. Police signals, 2. Traffic signals, 3. Road signs, 4. Rules (e.g. the priority-to-the-right rule). Police signals always override everything else.

question: If there are no speed limit signs, what are the basic default speed limits in Sweden?
options: 30 km/h built-up area, 50 km/h outside
50 km/h built-up area, 70 km/h outside
50 km/h built-up area, 90 km/h outside
70 km/h built-up area, 110 km/h outside
explanation: The book states the basic speed limits used when there are no signs: 50 km/h in a built-up area and 70 km/h outside of a built-up area.

question: On a road with no lane markings, how is a 'lane' legally defined?
options: Any strip of road at least 2 metres wide
A longitudinal field wide enough for one file of four-wheeled vehicles, with reasonable safety margins
Exactly half the width of the carriageway
Whatever width the driver personally judges to be safe
explanation: The Ordinance on Road Traffic Definitions defines a lane as wide enough for traffic in one file of four-wheeled vehicles, interpreted as requiring reasonable safety margins between vehicles, not vehicles packed closely together.

question: When is a driver prohibited from crossing into an adjacent lane due to lane markings?
options: When the line on their own side is solid
When the line on the other lane's side is solid
Whenever there is any centre line at all
Only on motorways
explanation: You are not permitted to pass over into another lane if the line on your side is solid. A driver on the side where the line is not solid may cross over, for example to overtake.

question: Which of the following is an explicit exception where the priority-to-the-right rule does NOT apply?
options: Entering a roundabout
Two cars merging in an open area with no signs
A junction where the Junction (A28) sign is displayed
A standard unsigned crossroads in a housing estate
explanation: The book lists exceptions where the priority-to-the-right rule does not apply: priority roads, functioning traffic signals, roundabouts, give way/obligation to stop signs, leaving an acceleration lane, reversing, and exits.

question: You are turning right on a green light. Pedestrians are crossing the road you are turning into, even though there is no marked pedestrian crossing there. Must you give way?
options: No, only marked crossings require giving way
Yes, the turning rule requires you not to obstruct pedestrians crossing the carriageway you are joining, marked or not
Only if the pedestrians are already halfway across
No, because you have a green light
explanation: The turning rule states you may not obstruct pedestrians or cyclists crossing the carriageway you are turning into, even without a marked pedestrian crossing, footpath, or bicycle path.

question: Under the exit rule, from which of the following must a driver give way when leaving?
options: A car park
A priority road onto a minor road
A roundabout
A motorway acceleration lane with no oncoming traffic
explanation: The exit rule gives an obligation to give way when exiting a car park, a property, a pedestrian street, home zone, bicycle street, hard shoulder, off-road area, or a footpath/bicycle path you have crossed.

question: At an uncontrolled bicycle crossing (sign B8), what is a driver's obligation toward cyclists who are on it or about to enter it?
options: No obligation; cyclists must give way to cars
An obligation to give way
Only need to slow down slightly, no obligation to stop or give way
The obligation only applies to moped drivers, not cyclists
explanation: At a bicycle crossing, a driver has an obligation to give way to cyclists and drivers of class II mopeds who are on, or about to enter, the bicycle crossing (Road Traffic Ordinance).

question: What distinguishes a controlled pedestrian crossing from an uncontrolled one?
options: Whether it has road markings
Whether it has functioning traffic signals or a police officer directing traffic
Whether it is located in a built-up area
Whether cyclists are also present
explanation: A pedestrian crossing is controlled if traffic is regulated by functioning traffic signals (or a police officer); otherwise it is uncontrolled and drivers must give way to pedestrians stepping out or about to do so.

question: What must a driver do when exiting a roundabout?
options: Nothing, no signalling is needed
Indicate right to signal the exit
Indicate left to warn others they are leaving
Come to a complete stop before exiting
explanation: You must indicate your intention to exit (i.e. to the right) when exiting the roundabout, per the book's driving-on-a-roundabout rules.

question: Who has priority when a vehicle wants to enter a roundabout?
options: The vehicle entering, over vehicles already on the roundabout
Vehicles already driving on the roundabout, over vehicles entering
Whoever arrives first, regardless of position
It follows the priority-to-the-right rule as normal
explanation: "A driver who is entering a roundabout is obliged to give way to every vehicle that is already driving on the roundabout." (Road Traffic Ordinance)

question: How close to a junction is stopping or parking generally prohibited?
options: 5 metres
10 metres
15 metres
20 metres
explanation: The book lists stopping/parking as prohibited at a junction and within 10 metres of it, among other locations.

question: You begin parking using a parking disc at 09:47. What time should you set on the disc?
explanation: The stated time on a parking disc must be set to the nearest subsequent half-hour from when parking commenced. Starting at 09:47, the nearest subsequent half-hour is 10:00.

question: According to the 'verge post' rule of thumb, what is a good following distance to maintain from the car in front on a country road?
options: 25 metres
50 metres
100 metres
150 metres
explanation: Verge posts on country roads are spaced 50 metres apart, and a good following distance is about 100 metres, corresponding to the distance between 3 verge posts.

question: When meeting oncoming traffic on a narrow country road at a passing place, who must stop?
options: Always the car on the right
The first car to arrive at the passing place
The car travelling downhill
Whichever car is larger
explanation: The first car to arrive at the passing place shall stop, irrespective of which side the passing place is on.

question: What is the maximum speed for a heavy lorry on a motorway or clearway?
options: 70 km/h
80 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
explanation: Heavy lorries may drive at a maximum of 90 km/h on motorways and clearways, and a maximum of 80 km/h on other roads.

question: Which of the following is true of clearways compared with motorways?
options: Clearways may have oncoming traffic but no intersecting traffic on the same level
Clearways allow intersecting traffic at junctions
Clearways offer no stopping/parking prohibitions unlike motorways
Clearways have a lower risk of accidents than motorways
explanation: A clearway is a mix of motorway and country road: no intersecting traffic, but oncoming traffic may occur (rarely, usually with cable barriers). Accidents actually occur more frequently than on motorways.

question: You are being overtaken by another vehicle. What are you required to do?
options: Speed up slightly to reduce the time spent side-by-side
Maintain your speed or slow down, and assist the overtaking car even if its manoeuvre was risky
Move fully onto the hard shoulder no matter what is there
Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic
explanation: When being overtaken you must not accelerate, and you are obliged to assist the overtaking car, even if the manoeuvre is prohibited or dangerous.

question: Your manual transmission car stalls on a level crossing and will not restart. What should you try first?
options: Wait for the barriers to lower fully, then push the car
Release the clutch, turn the key fully in the ignition and hold it so the starter motor pushes the car forward
Call 112 immediately without attempting to move the car
Reverse off the tracks at high speed
explanation: For a manual transmission car that won't start, release the clutch and hold the key turned as far as possible so the starter motor pushes the car forwards; calling 112 is the fallback if the car cannot be moved.

question: Is overtaking permitted at a level crossing that has traffic signals (red, amber, green) but no barriers?
options: No, overtaking is never allowed near a level crossing
Yes, all vehicles may be overtaken
Only two-wheeled vehicles may be overtaken
Only if the signal is flashing amber
explanation: Per the overtaking table, when there are no barriers but there are red/amber/green signals, all vehicles may be overtaken at the level crossing.

question: What is the maximum speed a driver may travel at in a home zone (sign E9)?
options: 20 km/h
Walking speed (around 7 km/h)
30 km/h
50 km/h
explanation: In a home zone you may drive no faster than walking speed, around 7 km/h, and must give way to pedestrians.

question: Which condition does the book describe as the most treacherous, and why?
options: Heavy snow and ice, because it's hard to see the road surface
Patches of hidden ice, because the danger isn't obvious to the driver
Rain, because visibility is reduced
Fog, because of reduced sight distance
explanation: A lot of snow and ice is not treacherous, as the danger is evident. Patches of ice are treacherous, as the danger is hidden from the driver.

question: What is 'overlearning' in the context of driving?
options: Learning too many rules to the point of confusion
Practising a skill until it becomes second nature, freeing attention for the surrounding environment
Studying beyond what is required for the theory test
Repeating the same mistake multiple times
explanation: Overlearning has taken place when something (like clutch work or gear shifting) has become second nature, so the driver can focus on everything happening around them.

question: What blood alcohol concentration defines ordinary (non-aggravated) drunk driving?
options: 0.1 per mille
0.2 per mille
0.5 per mille
1.0 per mille
explanation: Drunk driving is defined at 0.2 per mille (0.1 mg of alcohol per litre of breath); aggravated drunk driving starts at 1.0 per mille.

question: Which of the following is true regarding a hands-free mobile phone device while driving?
options: It removes all risk since your hands are free
Using a mobile phone is illegal regardless of hands-free use
The conversation itself can still be distracting even though your hands are free
Hands-free devices are only legal for GPS navigation
explanation: A hands-free device frees both hands, but the conversation itself is distracting; a complicated phone call can make you lose focus even with both hands on the wheel.

question: According to the book's statistics, during which time period do most tiredness-related accidents occur?
explanation: Most tiredness-related accidents occur between 02:00 and 05:00, according to the book's statistics on tiredness.

question: What percentage of your visual field is made up of peripheral vision?
explanation: Central vision makes up only 1-2% of the visual field; the remaining 98-99% is peripheral vision, which is impaired by alcohol and tiredness.

question: When you stop for a visually impaired pedestrian at a crossing, what should you avoid doing?
options: Stopping in good time before the crossing
Revving your engine or honking your horn unnecessarily
Waiting until they have fully crossed before moving off
Staying quiet while they cross
explanation: You should be careful not to make noise: do not rev your engine, and only honk if there is an emergency, since a visually impaired person relies on sound cues.

question: Why can a child be harder to spot near traffic than an adult, according to the book?
options: Children always wear dark clothing
Children are small enough to be completely hidden behind a parked car, unlike adults
Children never look both ways before crossing
Children are legally required to stay off roads
explanation: In most cases an adult can be spotted behind a parked car, but a child can be completely hidden by the car, giving no warning before they step into the street.

question: According to the book's accident statistics, roughly what percentage of traffic deaths involved a person not wearing a seatbelt?
explanation: The book states that 40% of all those killed in traffic were not wearing a seat belt.

question: Which of these vehicle categories is subject to 'the speed limit of the road' rather than a separate fixed maximum speed?
options: Heavy lorry on other roads (capped at 80 km/h)
Moped class I (capped at 45 km/h)
Private car and light lorry
A motor vehicle towing an unbraked trailer exceeding half the pulling vehicle's weight
explanation: According to the book's speed table, private cars, light lorries, motorcycles and light buses are simply subject to whatever speed limit applies to the road, unlike categories with their own fixed caps.

question: If you double your speed (with reaction time unchanged), how does your reaction distance change?
options: It doubles
It quadruples
It stays the same
It increases by 50%
explanation: Reaction distance increases proportionally with speed: 2x higher speed means 2x longer reaction distance.

question: If you triple your speed, how does your braking distance change (assuming the same road and tyre conditions)?
options: It triples
It increases sixfold
It increases ninefold
It stays the same
explanation: Braking distance increases quadratically with speed (raised to the power of 2): 3x higher speed means 9x longer braking distance.

question: What is the legal period during which winter tyres are mandatory in winter road conditions?
options: 1 November - 31 March
1 December - 31 March
1 October - 30 April
1 December - 28 February
explanation: The legal requirement for winter tyres in winter road conditions runs from 1 December to 31 March.

question: If your car has studded tyres, what is required of a trailer being towed behind it in winter conditions?
options: The trailer must also have studded tyres
The trailer must use friction tyres instead
There is no requirement; only the car's tyres matter
The trailer must use summer tyres to balance ball pressure
explanation: If the car has studded tyres, a trailer connected to it must also have studded tyres in winter conditions, to avoid the risk of the trailer jack-knifing due to a grip mismatch.

question: What does electronic stability control (ESC) do?
options: Increases fuel efficiency automatically
Detects wheel spin or excessive turning and applies corrective braking to individual wheels
Automatically inflates the tyres to the correct pressure
Prevents the car from exceeding the posted speed limit
explanation: ESC uses sensors to detect if a wheel is spinning or the car is turning too sharply, then calculates corrective measures such as braking a specific wheel.

question: What does it most likely mean if the brake pedal keeps sinking slowly even after reaching the bottom?
options: Air in the brake system
A leak in the brake system
Normally worn brake pads only
A fully functioning brake servo
explanation: If the pedal continues to sink slowly despite reaching the bottom, this indicates a probable leak in the brake system, which poses a serious traffic hazard.

question: From roughly what speed can a frontal airbag be triggered?
explanation: Airbags are triggered at speeds over 20-30 km/h, and take just 0.1 seconds to fill up.

question: Until when should a baby car seat (for a child aged roughly 0-9 months) typically be used?
options: Until the child can sit steadily on their own
Until the child is exactly 1 year old, regardless of development
Until the child reaches 135 cm in height
Until the child can talk
explanation: A baby car seat is for children aged 0-9 months old, or until the child is able to sit steadily.

question: What is the maximum total width, including any protruding load, permitted for a vehicle on a normal public road?
options: 200 cm
230 cm
260 cm
300 cm
explanation: The total width, including load, may be a maximum of 260 cm (2.6 m) for driving on normal roads; wider vehicles may only use private roads.

question: A car with a total weight of 3,200 kg tows a trailer whose own total weight is 700 kg. Is this trailer classed as 'light' under a regular category B licence?
options: Yes, because the trailer's own total weight is under 750 kg
No, because the combined weight exceeds 3,500 kg
No, because trailer brakes are required above 500 kg
Yes, but only with the extended B96 licence
explanation: A trailer with a maximum total weight of 750 kg or less is always classed as light, regardless of the combined weight with the car - point 2 (the 3,500 kg combined limit) only applies if point 1 is not met.

question: What is the minimum load-securing requirement fastenings must withstand in the forward direction, as a percentage of cargo weight?
explanation: Fastenings must withstand a movement of at least 80% of the cargo weight in the forward direction, and 50% backwards and to the sides.

question: Which combination of lights is prohibited under the rules described in the book?
options: Dipped headlights + parking lights
Dipped headlights + fog lights
Full beam headlights alone at night on an unlit road
Rear fog light alone in heavy rain
explanation: The book explicitly lists dipped headlights + fog lights as a prohibited combination, along with dipped headlights + daytime running lights and dipped headlights + auxiliary high beam lights.

question: During an internal safety check, what should happen to the brake pedal when you turn the steering wheel slightly and start the car, to test the power steering?
options: It should remain completely rigid and not move at all
It should sink slightly and the steering wheel should become easier to turn
It should vibrate rapidly
It should rise upward on its own
explanation: When starting the car with the brake pedal depressed and turning the wheel slightly, the pedal sinking and the wheel becoming easier to turn confirms the power steering and servo are functioning.

question: A car's second roadworthiness inspection was completed in June 2024. By when must the next (third) inspection be completed?
options: No later than June 2025
No later than August 2025
No later than December 2025
No later than June 2026
explanation: Subsequent inspections after the second must be conducted no later than 14 months after the month of the most recent inspection, and the deadline is always the last day of that month - June 2024 plus 14 months lands on 31 August 2025.

question: Your engine has been running and the coolant level is too low. What should you do?
options: Open the radiator cap immediately to top up coolant
Avoid opening the radiator while the engine is warm, as hot steam may burn you
Pour cold water directly onto the hot engine block
Ignore it, since coolant does not need topping up
explanation: You should not open the radiator when the engine is warm, as it may release very hot steam and cause burns; the radiator must instead be replenished with coolant (water and glycol) once safe to do so.

question: What is Part 2 of the vehicle registration certificate primarily used for?
options: Ordering registration plates
Change of ownership and deregistration
Notifying on-road status only
Storing insurance policy details
explanation: Part 2 of the registration certificate contains ownership information and is used for change of ownership and deregistration, so it should be stored safely rather than left in the glove compartment.

question: Which level of car insurance covers damage to your OWN car after an accident you caused?
options: Third-party insurance
Partial insurance
Fully comprehensive insurance
None of these levels ever cover this
explanation: Fully comprehensive insurance (motor vehicle damage insurance) covers damage to your own car in a traffic accident, on top of everything covered by third-party and partial insurance.

question: Roughly what percentage of harmful substances in exhaust fumes do catalytic converters eliminate?
explanation: Catalytic converters transform harmful exhaust substances into carbon dioxide and water, eliminating 80-95% of the harmful substances, once they reach their 400-600 degree C operating temperature.

question: When engine braking, at what RPM should you shift to a lower gear to keep fuel consumption at zero?
options: Just before 800-900 rpm
Just before 1,200-1,300 rpm
Just before 2,000-2,100 rpm
Just before 2,500 rpm
explanation: You should shift down just before the rpm falls to 1,200-1,300, since below that level the engine starts consuming fuel again.

question: What is required for a vehicle to be allowed to drive in a Class 3 environmental zone?
options: Any Euro 6 diesel or petrol car
Only electric, fuel cell, or gas vehicles - petrol, diesel and even plug-in hybrids are prohibited
Any car fitted with a catalytic converter
Only heavy vehicles meeting Euro 6
explanation: In a Class 3 environmental zone, only electric vehicles, fuel cell vehicles and gas vehicles are allowed; petrol and diesel are prohibited, and plug-in hybrids are also prohibited.

question: What does a road sign with the code A28 indicate?
options: Roundabout ahead
Junction
Give way
Priority road
explanation: A28 is the Junction sign, sometimes displayed to clarify that the priority-to-the-right rule applies at a particularly difficult junction.

question: Which sign code corresponds to 'Priority road'?
options: B1
B4
B5
E9
explanation: B4 is the Priority road sign, normally displayed after every junction on a priority road; B5 is Priority road ends, and B1 is Give way.

question: What category of sign do codes prefixed with the letter 'C' belong to?
options: Warning signs
Priority signs
Prohibitory signs
Mandatory signs
explanation: Signs prefixed 'C' are prohibitory signs (e.g. C27 No overtaking, C39 No stopping or parking), distinct from 'A' warning signs, 'B' priority signs, and 'D' mandatory signs.

question: According to the mnemonic rule for direction arrow signs, what does a diagonal (slanting) arrow indicate?
options: The direction you must follow
Which lane to use to pass (this side)
A warning of a junction ahead
A mandatory stop
explanation: The mnemonic rule is: diagonal (twisted/slanting) arrows mean pass on this side, indicating the correct lane; horizontal/vertical straight arrows mean the direction to be followed.

question: Which sign code is used for 'Give way'?
options: B1
B2
B3
B6
explanation: B1 is the Give way sign; B2 is Obligation to stop, and B3 is Pedestrian crossing.

question: Which category of sign is E9 ('Home zone') part of?
options: Warning signs (A)
Prohibitory signs (C)
Instruction signs (E)
Mandatory signs (D)
explanation: E9 (Home zone) belongs to the 'Instruction signs' (E) category, alongside signs like E1 Motorway, E5 Built-up area, and E7 Pedestrian street.

question: Which sign code is displayed at the actual entrance to a roundabout, obliging drivers to give way to traffic already circulating?
options: D3
B4
E9
explanation: D3 is the Roundabout sign displayed at the entrance itself, obliging entering drivers to give way; A30 (Roundabout ahead) is instead an advance warning sign further back.

question: What does the sign code C39 represent?
options: No parking
No stopping or parking
Date parking
No overtaking
explanation: C39 is the No stopping or parking sign; C35 is the separate No parking sign, which permits stopping but not parking.

question: A driver's speedometer was faulty and showed 75 km/h while the car was actually travelling at 90 km/h. How did the court rule?
options: The driver was not liable, since they trusted the speedometer
The driver was found guilty of speeding regardless of not knowing about the fault
The case was dismissed for lack of evidence
Only the vehicle manufacturer was held liable
explanation: The supreme court considered this to be speeding even though the driver was not aware of the problem with the speedometer - drivers remain responsible for their actual speed.

question: A driver parked where parking was prohibited because they had run out of fuel. What did the court rule?
options: The fine was cancelled since running out of fuel is an emergency
The driver was still liable, as drivers must ensure their vehicle has enough fuel
The driver only had to pay a reduced fine
Fuel gauges were ruled unreliable, so no fine applied
explanation: The court of appeal ruled that running out of fuel does not give a driver the right to leave their car in a prohibited parking place; drivers must ensure they have enough fuel.

question: A driver stopped their car, where stopping was prohibited, specifically to help push a broken-down car out of the road. What was the outcome?
options: The driver was fined, since stopping there was prohibited regardless of reason
The parking fine was cancelled, since the driver stopped to clear the road and make it accessible
The driver was charged with obstruction
The case set no legal precedent
explanation: The court of appeal cancelled the parking fine, as the driver had stopped in order to clear the road and make it accessible, which is a recognised exception to the stopping prohibition.
